title: Phase 1 · Stage 4: Remembering books
summary: Store the catalog in a list, find books, reject duplicate ISBNs with a set, and count authors with a dictionary.

steps.title: From counters to a catalog
body: Shelfwise counts books but forgets them the moment they are added. To list or search the catalog it has to **keep** each book. One book is five values that belong together; a **named tuple** holds them without writing a class yet (that is Phase 2):
var books = new List<(string Isbn, string Title, string Author, int Year, int Copies)>();

A `List<T>` grows as you add, keeps insertion order and is indexed from 0. The counters `books`, `copies` and `oldest` can go: every number can now be **computed from the list** when `stats` asks for it, so they can never drift out of step with the data.

code: var books = new List<(string Title, int Copies)>();
foreach (var b in books) total += b.Copies;
steps.explain: Three items, 2 + 1 + 4 copies, and index 1 is the second item.

steps.title: Keep the catalog in a list
prompt: Store every accepted book in a `List` of named tuples `(string Isbn, string Title, string Author, int Year, int Copies)` and remove the `books`, `copies` and `oldest` counters: `Stats()` computes its numbers from the list with a loop. All earlier output stays the same.
New commands (add them to `help` in this order: `Commands: add, list, find, stats, fine, help, quit`):

- `list` prints every book in the order added, as `isbn | title | author | year | 3 copies` (`1 copy` for one: write a small `string Copies(int n)` helper, because `Plural` would say *copys*). With no books: `No books yet.`
- `find <text>` prints every book whose title or author **contains** the text, ignoring case, in the same format. With no match: `No books match "<text>".`

require.message: Keeps the books in a List of named tuples

hints: Declare `var books = new List<(string Isbn, string Title, string Author, int Year, int Copies)>();` and in `AddBook` replace the counting with `books.Add((parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], year, count));`.
`Stats()` loops over `books`, summing `Copies` and tracking the smallest `Year`. The count is `books.Count`.
A shared `PrintBooks(list, whenEmpty)` serves both `list` and `find`. Matching is `book.Title.Contains(text, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || book.Author.Contains(...)`.

steps.title: Sets and dictionaries
body: Two books with the same ISBN are a data error: which one does a loan refer to? Checking with a loop over the list works, but gets slower as the catalog grows. A **HashSet** answers *have I seen this?* in one step, however big it is:
A **Dictionary** maps a key to a value. Counting things is its classic job:
names.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);      // a dictionary has no guaranteed order: sort for output

steps.prompt: Pick the collection for each job.
pairs: the catalog, in the order books were added
how many books each author has
the five fields of one ~add~ line
steps.explain: A list keeps order, a set answers membership questions, a dictionary looks up a value by key, and an array is a fixed-size row of values.

steps.prompt: `isbns` is a `HashSet<string>` that already holds `"978-1"`. What does `isbns.Add("978-1")` return, and how many items does the set hold afterwards?
steps.explain: A set never holds duplicates; `Add` reports whether the value was new. That makes it a check and a record in one call.

steps.title: Duplicates and authors
prompt: 1. Keep a `HashSet<string>` of the ISBNs in the catalog. `add` with an ISBN that is already there prints `Error: ISBN <isbn> is already in the catalog` and adds nothing. (Check this after the other validation.)
2. New command `authors`: one line per author, **sorted by name** (ordinal), as `<author>: <n> book(s)` (`1 book`, `2 books`). Count with a `Dictionary<string, int>`. With no books: `No books yet.`
3. `help` becomes `Commands: add, list, find, authors, stats, fine, help, quit`.

require.message: Counts authors in a Dictionary<string, int>

hints: `HashSet.Add` returns `false` when the value was already there, so it checks and records in one call: `if (!isbns.Add(parts[0])) return ...;`.
Put the set check after `ValidateBook`, so a rejected book does not reserve its ISBN.

Count with `perAuthor[book.Author] = perAuthor.GetValueOrDefault(book.Author) + 1;`, copy the keys into a `List<string>`, `Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal)` it, then print `$"{name}: {Plural(perAuthor[name], "book")}"`.
